hmmt-feb-2002-alg-01.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2002-alg-01.body:
If the median is $m$, the five largest numbers are each at least $m$, so the sum is at least $5m$. Thus $90\ge5m$, $m\le18$. This is attained by four $0$'s and five $18$'s.

**Answer: 18**

hmmt-feb-2002-alg-02.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2002-alg-02.body:
Write $p+q=x^2$, $p+7q=y^2$ with $x,y>0$. Then $6q=y^2-x^2=(y-x)(y+x)$. The factors have the same parity and the product is even, so both are even and $4\mid 6q$, forcing $q$ even, $q=2$. Then $(y-x)(y+x)=12$ with both even gives $y-x=2$, $y+x=6$, so $x=2$ and $p=x^2-q=2$.

**Answer: 2**

hmmt-feb-2002-alg-03.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2002-alg-03.body:
Multiply the two equations: $(a+b+c)\left(\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c\right)=3+\left(\frac ab+\frac ba+\frac ac+\frac ca+\frac bc+\frac cb\right)=26\cdot28=728$. So the sum is $728-3=725$.

**Answer: 725**

hmmt-feb-2002-alg-04.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2002-alg-04.body:
$864=2^5\cdot3^3$ and $1944=2^3\cdot3^5$. A multiple $864k$ is divisible by $1944$ iff $2^3\cdot3^5\mid 2^5\cdot 3^3 k$, i.e. iff $9\mid k$. A random multiple has $9\mid k$ with probability $\tfrac19$.

**Answer: 1/9**

hmmt-feb-2002-alg-05.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2002-alg-05.body:
$2002+2$ divides $2002^2-2^2$, so any common divisor of the first two terms divides $(2002^2+2)-(2002^2-4)=6$. Conversely every term is even, and the $n$th term is $\equiv1^n+2\equiv0\pmod 3$ since $2002\equiv1\pmod3$. So $6$ divides every term and the gcd is $6$.

**Answer: 6**

hmmt-feb-2002-alg-06.title: Factor out 2
hmmt-feb-2002-alg-06.body:
Even divisors of $1000$ are $2k$ with $k\mid500=2^2\cdot5^3$. The sum of divisors of $500$ is $(1+2+4)(1+5+25+125)=7\cdot156=1092$, so the answer is $2\cdot1092=2184$.

**Answer: 2184**

hmmt-feb-2002-alg-06.title: Subtract odd divisors
hmmt-feb-2002-alg-06.body:
All divisors of $1000$ sum to $(1+2+4+8)(156)=15\cdot156=2340$; the odd ones sum to $156$. So $2340-156=2184$.

**Answer: 2184**

hmmt-feb-2002-alg-07.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2002-alg-07.body:
Let $s=x+y+z+w$. The equations say $s+x=1$, $s+2y=2$, $s+3z=3$, $s+4w=25$. So $x=1-s$, $y=\frac{2-s}2$, $z=\frac{3-s}3$, $w=\frac{25-s}4$. Adding: $s=1+1+1+\frac{25}{4}-s\left(1+\frac12+\frac13+\frac14\right)=\frac{37}{4}-\frac{25}{12}s$, so $\frac{37}{12}s=\frac{37}{4}$, $s=3$. Then $w=\frac{25-3}{4}=\frac{11}2$.

**Answer: 11/2**

hmmt-feb-2002-alg-09.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2002-alg-09.body:
If $n$ is even, $n+1$ just changes the last $0$ to $1$, so $f(n+1)=f(n)+1$. If $n$ is odd, adding $1$ turns the final block of $1$'s into $0$'s and the $0$ before it into a $1$; the count of ones is unchanged iff that block of ones has length exactly $1$, i.e. $n$ ends in $01$ in binary, i.e. $n\equiv1\pmod4$. In $1\le n\le2002$ these are $1,5,\dots,2001$: $501$ values.

**Answer: 501**

hmmt-feb-2002-alg-10.title: Solution
hmmt-feb-2002-alg-10.body:
Let $T_n$ be the value of the nested expression beginning with $n$, so $T_2=2$ and $T_n=n+\tfrac12T_{n-1}$. Then $T_3=4$, $T_4=6$, and by induction $T_n=2n-2$: indeed $n+\tfrac12(2n-4)=2n-2$. Hence $T_{2002}=4002$.

**Answer: 4002**
